about: Banter: exchanges between the voices, each a few turns of [voice, text], for quiet passages (lull) and quiet overs ending (betweenOvers). Never over a wicket, a boundary or a finish. The one who opens is never the over's caller; the caller may answer.

exchanges: THAT'S DRINKS, BY THE LOOK OF IT. I COULD MURDER A CUP OF TEA.
YOU SAID THAT AN HOUR AGO, BILL. AND YOU HAD ONE.
I'VE BEEN WATCHING THE FIELD SETTINGS. FASCINATING STUFF.
YOU'VE BEEN WATCHING THE PIE STAND, TONY.
A QUIET OVER. ONE OF THE GAME'S UNDERRATED PLEASURES.
QUIET FOR YOU, RICHIE. BILL'S BEEN SHOUTING AT A PIGEON.
LOOK AT THE CROWD! THEY'RE DOING THE WAVE!
SO THEY ARE. IT'S COME ROUND TWICE AND MISSED US BOTH TIMES.
IN MY DAY WE BOWLED TWENTY OVERS BEFORE LUNCH.
IN YOUR DAY THE BALL WAS STITCHED BY HAND, TONY!
THE UMPIRE HAS CHANGED HIS HAT.
RICHIE, THAT'S THE MOST EXCITING THING YOU'VE SAID ALL DAY!
I'VE GOT A GOOD FEELING ABOUT THE NEXT OVER!
YOU SAID THAT ABOUT THE LAST SIX, BILL.
THEY'LL BE CHECKING THE BALL. IT'S GONE A LITTLE SOFT.

turns: THE MUSIC'S UP BETWEEN OVERS! I LOVE IT!
I'D LOVE IT TOO, BILL, IF I COULD HEAR MYSELF THINK.
A LOVELY DAY FOR IT. THE SHADOWS, THE QUIET.
THE QUIET! RICHIE, I'VE BEEN ASLEEP SINCE TEA!

exchanges: THAT'S THE BOWLERS WINNING, BILL. QUIETLY.
THE PIGEONS AT FINE LEG HAVEN'T MOVED IN AN HOUR.
THEY'RE BETTER AT LEAVING THAN SOME BATTERS I KNOW!
DOT, DOT, DOT. SOMEONE HAS TO BREAK THIS.
FORTY. ONE OF THEM IS A CRISP PACKET, BILL.

turns: SOME OF US ARE GETTING OLDER WATCHING IT.
THREE DOTS IN A ROW IN A T20! THE CROWD'S RESTLESS!
SO IS THE BATTER. THAT'S WHEN THE MISTAKE COMES.
